metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: The constant presence of one's past, inner thoughts, or companion-like aspects of oneself that accompany them through life.
acceptable_visual_variants: A person walking on a sunny path with a long, soft shadow stretching beside them
A silhouette of a person overlapping with a soft, stylized shadow on a wall
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: Every shadow walks along with you
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: An illustrator might draw a literal dark silhouette walking hand-in-hand with a person, which looks like a ghost or a separate entity rather than a natural shadow.
metaphor_spans.tenor: The constant, inseparable presence of one's inner self or past
metaphor_spans.vehicle: A shadow walking as a companion
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Depict a person walking in bright sunlight with their natural shadow cast clearly on the ground beside them, mimicking their posture.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: The deep, hidden, or subconscious levels of human consciousness and thoughts.
acceptable_visual_variants: Overlapping translucent waves of soft blue and golden light
A stylized silhouette of a head filled with deep, layered shades of color
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: Every deep layer of the mind
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Drawing a physical brain with literal geological or fabric layers inside it would look bizarre and overly anatomical.
metaphor_spans.source_span_translation: Each deep layer of the mind
metaphor_spans.tenor: The subconscious or deep levels of human thoughts and emotions
metaphor_spans.vehicle: Physical layers or strata (like soil or fabric)
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Use abstract visual metaphors like overlapping translucent sheets of light or water depths to represent layers of consciousness.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The translation collapses the grammatical gender agreement of 'bharta hai' (masculine singular verb form) which agrees with the masculine noun 'man' (mind), rendering it as a passive/stative 'Feels filled' which loses the active, gender-marked aspect of the Hindi verb.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: New hopes and positive expectations beginning to grow, develop, and flourish in a person's life.
acceptable_visual_variants: A close-up of fresh green shoots and small buds opening under morning sunlight
A person opening a window to let in bright sunlight, with potted plants blooming on the sill
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Depicting literal flowers with the word 'hope' written on them, or human figures growing out of flower buds, which looks cartoonish.
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Show a person looking up at the morning sun with a bright, hopeful expression, surrounded by naturally opening flower buds in a garden.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The translation renders 'khilti hain' (plural verb) as 'bloom' and 'panapta hai' (singular verb) as 'flourishes', but loses the subtle rhythmic and phonetic resonance of the parallel structures 'khilti hain' and 'panapta hai' in the Hindi original.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: The feeling of complete fulfillment and realization of one's deepest desires and aspirations.
acceptable_visual_variants: A person standing on a hilltop looking out over a vast, beautiful valley illuminated by a golden sunrise
A warm, glowing scene of a person looking at their hands or surroundings with a sense of wonder and peace
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: As if all dreams take physical form
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Showing literal dream bubbles containing random objects (like cars or houses) solidifying into reality, which misses the emotional and poetic sense of inner peace.
metaphor_spans.source_span_translation: As if all dreams come true
metaphor_spans.tenor: A profound sense of joy, clarity, and fulfillment in the present moment
metaphor_spans.vehicle: Dreams taking physical shape or form
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Depict a serene, beautiful landscape bathed in golden light, evoking a dreamlike yet real and peaceful atmosphere.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The translation of 'sakar hon' as 'come true' loses the literal Sanskrit-derived meaning of 'sakar' (taking concrete form / shape), flattening a visual metaphor of physical manifestation into a generic English idiom.

annotation.theme: The transformative power of light and hope in renewing the inner mind and outer world

original_poem:
उजालों की धूप में,  
हर साया संग चलता है।  
मन की हर गहरी परत,  
जैसे रोशनी से भरता है।

सूरज की हर किरण में,  
उम्मीदें नई खिलती हैं।  
आसमान की हर छांव में,  
एक नया जीवन पनपता है।

उजालों की इस धूप में,  
हर रंग नया सा लगता है।  
जैसे सारे सपने साकार हों,  
इस अनोखी छवि के संग।
translated_poem:
In the sunshine of brightness,  
Every shadow walks alongside.  
Each deep layer of the mind,  
Feels filled with light.

In every ray of the sun,  
New hopes bloom.  
In every shade of the sky,  
A new life flourishes.

In this sunshine of brightness,  
Every color seems renewed.  
As if all dreams come true,  
In this unique scene.
